entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0414: Exponential event growth with `ENABLE_WIKILINKS`
entry.content:
Exponential event growth with `ENABLE_WIKILINKS`

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • pulldown-cmark — fixed in 0.13.5

When `Options::ENABLE_WIKILINKS` is enabled, a wikilink with a pipe separator and empty display text, such as `[[a|]]`, leaks its child node's sibling chain into the content that follows it. Each such link roughly doubles the number of events the parser yields for the rest of the document, so output grows exponentially with input size: 16 repetitions of `[[a|]] ` (112 bytes) yield 327,676 events, where the fixed parser yields 65. A document of a few kilobytes is enough to exhaust memory in a process that collects the events or renders them to HTML. Applications that parse untrusted Markdown with `ENABLE_WIKILINKS` set, including through `Options::all()`, are affected. The option is off by default. Parsing without it is not affected. The flaw was fixed in [#1102](https://github.com/pulldo…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-796p-j2gh-9m2q: dcap-qvl has Missing Verification for QE Identity
entry.content:
dcap-qvl has Missing Verification for QE Identity

Aliases: CVE-2026-22696, PYSEC-2026-326

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • dcap-qvl — fixed in 0.3.9
  • @phala/dcap-qvl — fixed in 0.3.9
  • @phala/dcap-qvl-web
  • @phala/dcap-qvl-node
  • dcap-qvl — fixed in 0.3.9

## Impact This vulnerability involves a critical gap in the cryptographic verification process within the dcap-qvl. The library fetches QE Identity collateral (including qe_identity, qe_identity_signature, and qe_identity_issuer_chain) from the PCCS. However, it skips to verify the QE Identity signature against its certificate chain and does not enforce policy constraints on the QE Report. ## Consequences An attacker can forge the QE Identity data to whitelist a malicious or non-Intel Quoting Enclave. This allows the attacker to forge the QE and sign untrusted quotes that the verifier will accept as valid. Effectively, this bypasses the entire remote attestation security model, as the verifier can no longer trust the entity responsible for signing the quotes. ## Who is impacted All depl…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-w44r-93j7-qv28: rustls: An unauthenticated ServerHello poisons the per-name key-exchange record, so later ClientHellos carry only a classical X25519 share
entry.content:
rustls: An unauthenticated ServerHello poisons the per-name key-exchange record, so later ClientHellos carry only a classical X25519 share

Aliases: RUSTSEC-2026-0349

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • rustls — fixed in 0.23.46
  • rustls — fixed in 0.24.0-dev.2

## Summary The client records the server-selected key-exchange group per server name when it processes the ServerHello, before the server is authenticated. A network attacker can answer one connection attempt for a target name with a ServerHello that selects X25519 and close the connection. Later ClientHellos for that name carry one X25519 share while supported_groups still lists X25519MLKEM768 first. If the server accepts that share instead of sending a HelloRetryRequest, the handshake completes with classical key exchange only and no error. An attacker that answers one connection attempt for the target name with a ServerHello selecting X25519 changes every later ClientHello of that client for that name, for as long as the entry stays in the store. No certificate or completed handshake …

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-h2v8-394m-p7vv: Rustls: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate an attacker-controlled amount of memory up to 1 GiB before authentication.
entry.content:
Rustls: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate an attacker-controlled amount of memory up to 1 GiB before authentication.

Aliases: RUSTSEC-2026-0348

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • rustls — fixed in 0.23.46
  • rustls — fixed in 0.24.0-dev.2

### Summary The built-in (but disabled by default) Brotli certificate decoder bounds the output buffer but accepts an input-selected history window. A header of five bytes can specify a 1 GiB window allocation. A peer can abort a process whose allocator cannot satisfy that request. A client must enable Brotli and connect to the peer; a server must enable Brotli and request a client certificate. Neither direction requires a trusted attacker certificate. ### Details rustls calls `BrotliDecompress` which enables Brotli's large-window extension. rustls applies a limit to certificates, but this applies to the decompressed result, and not to any internal allocations the process requires. ### Impact Client applications that enable the `brotli` feature will be vulnerable to malicious servers.…

rustls: ECH rejection can expose buffered application data to authenticated outer server before `ech_required` alert

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0413: Use-after-free of caller-owned server name in client connection constructors
entry.content:
Use-after-free of caller-owned server name in client connection constructors

Aliases: GHSA-rc3f-4j82-cmrg

Affected:

  • rustls-ffi — fixed in 0.15.7

In rustls-ffi 0.12.0 through 0.15.6, `rustls_client_connection_new()` and `rustls_client_connection_new_alpn()` retained a reference to the caller's `server_name` buffer after returning, rather than copying it. The API documentation did not require the buffer to outlive the call and as a result if the caller freed or reused the buffer, later TLS processing read freed memory. Clients that free or reuse the `server_name` buffer after the constructor returns are affected. This is most likely for language bindings that pass temporary strings. Callers that keep the `server_name` buffer alive for the lifetime of the `rustls_client_config` are not affected. Versions 0.12.0 through 0.15.6 are affected. Version 0.15.7+ changed these APIs to copy the input buffer.

  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0413.html

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0395: Use-after-free with `CParameter::StableInBuffer`
entry.content:
Use-after-free with `CParameter::StableInBuffer`

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

With `CParameter::StableInBuffer(true)` (`experimental` feature), the C library keeps a pointer to the input of one streaming call and reads from it in later calls, including `flush_stream` and `end_stream`, which take no input. An `InBuffer` only borrows its slice for one call, so safe code could free it in between, and freed memory was compressed into the frame. The C library behaves this way since zstd 1.5.4, whether bundled or linked from the system. The flaw was corrected by refusing to enable the parameter.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/zstd-safe
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0395.html
  • https://github.com/gyscos/zstd-rs/commit/53a8a290d8cfb52ff5b29fb6e04a40b5a174cc65

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0392: Uninitialized memory exposed by `write::Decoder` on a corrupt legacy frame
entry.content:
Uninitialized memory exposed by `write::Decoder` on a corrupt legacy frame

Affected:

  • zstd — fixed in 0.8.0

From 0.4.22 to 0.7.x, the writer behind `zstd::stream::write::Decoder` set its output buffer's length to its full capacity before each decompression call, then to the position the call reported, and only checked for an error afterwards. When decompression fails inside a legacy (zstd v0.4 to v0.7) frame, the bundled zstd library reports the output as fully written although nothing was written, so stale heap memory, up to the buffer size (32 KiB by default), was passed to the wrapped writer. Legacy support is enabled by default, and a few bytes of corrupt legacy frame are enough. Whether this reaches an attacker depends on where the application sends the decompressed output. From 0.8.0, the writer uses zstd-safe's buffers, and the same flaw there is covered by the zstd-safe advisory for it…

  • https://crates.io/crates/zstd

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0399: Use-after-free through `init_using_cdict` and `init_using_ddict`
entry.content:
Use-after-free through `init_using_cdict` and `init_using_ddict`

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

`CCtx::init_using_cdict` and `DCtx::init_using_ddict` (`experimental` feature, deprecated) took the dictionary as `&CDict<'b>` and `&DDict<'b>` with only `'b: 'a`, so the dictionary itself could be dropped while the context still pointed at it. The same mistake in other constructors was fixed earlier (<https://github.com/gyscos/zstd-rs/issues/365>). The flaw was corrected by taking `&'a CDict<'b>` and `&'a DDict<'b>`.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/zstd-safe

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0396: `Seekable` reads a NULL or out-of-bounds seek table
entry.content:
`Seekable` reads a NULL or out-of-bounds seek table

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

`Seekable` did not record whether it was initialized. On a fresh `Seekable`, or one whose `init_buff()` failed, `decompress`, `offset_to_frame_index` and `frame_decompressed_size` made the C library read a NULL seek table. After a failed re-initialization, `decompress` returned data from the refused buffer using the previous seek table. Separately, `frame_decompressed_size(num_frames())`, on `Seekable` and `SeekTable`, read one entry past the end of the seek table. The flaw was corrected by refusing to use a `Seekable` until an initialization succeeded, and by checking the frame index.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/zstd-safe
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0396.html
  • https://github.com/gyscos/zstd-rs/commit/a9626069d6f2e90b782b8f627f57a361cfe8ef85
  • https://github.com/gyscos/zstd-rs/pull/384

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0410: WebAssembly allocator shim corrupts memory on allocation failure
entry.content:
WebAssembly allocator shim corrupts memory on allocation failure

Affected:

  • zstd-sys — fixed in 2.1.2

On wasm32, zstd-sys provides `malloc` and `free` to the C library through a shim over Rust's allocator. The shim did not check for allocation failure: it wrote its size header to address 0 and returned address 4, which the C library used as a valid buffer. `free(NULL)` also read below address 0. Whenever the instance cannot grow its memory by what a frame asks for, a small crafted frame (a 9-byte header declaring a 128 MiB window is enough) made decompression write decoded data over the bottom of the module's linear memory, instead of failing. The corruption stays within the wasm sandbox. The flaw was corrected by returning NULL on allocation failure or size overflow, and by making `free(NULL)` a no-op.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/zstd-sys
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0410.html
  • https://github.com/gyscos/zstd-rs/commit/165d1625553c236b9700ca794b8a7c51f5d98314

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0403: Uninitialized memory exposed when streaming decompression of a legacy frame fails
entry.content:
Uninitialized memory exposed when streaming decompression of a legacy frame fails

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

When decompression fails inside a legacy (zstd v0.4 to v0.7) frame, the bundled zstd library reports the output buffer as fully written although nothing was written. `DCtx::decompress_stream` committed that position even on error, and for a `Vec<u8>` destination this extended the vector's length over uninitialized memory. Legacy support is enabled by default. A 5- or 6-byte corrupt legacy frame is enough: through `zstd::stream::write::Decoder`, up to 32 KiB of stale heap memory is then passed to the wrapped writer on the next `write()` or `flush()`, or when an `auto_flush()`/`on_flush()` decoder is dropped. Whether this reaches an attacker depends on where the application sends the decompressed output. `zstd::stream::read::Decoder`, `zstd::decode_all` and the bulk API are not affected. B…

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0400: Use-after-free of a dictionary after a one-shot call on a context with an open stream
entry.content:
Use-after-free of a dictionary after a one-shot call on a context with an open stream

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

The one-shot `DCtx` and `CCtx` methods assumed the C library resets the context, but it leaves an open stream as it is. When a stream was left unfinished on a context, a one-shot call such as `decompress_using_dict` could leave the context pointing at the dictionary borrowed for that call, and the next streaming call resumed the stream against it after it was freed: decompressed output then contained freed heap memory. On the compression side, the stream resumed against the one-shot call's buffers. This requires an application to use one context for both streaming and one-shot calls without a reset in between. The flaw was corrected by resetting the session after one-shot calls whenever a stream may be open.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/zstd-safe
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0400.html
  • https://github.com/gyscos/zstd-rs/commit/d34502a0ed07f80ab2aa4c65059578e0466f2467

Build environment compiled into the library and readable at runtime

Affected:

  • rustpython-vm — fixed in 0.6.0

The build script of `rustpython-vm` 0.3.0 through 0.5.0 writes every environment variable of the build into `$OUT_DIR/env_vars.rs`. The crate compiles that file into `_sysconfigdata`'s `build_time_vars`. That module is always compiled. A binary built in CI with secrets in the environment carries those secrets in clear text. Registry tokens, cloud credentials and API keys are the usual ones. Anyone with the binary can read them with `strings` or from Python. Version 0.6.0 removes the dump and the include. Users of earlier versions should upgrade, rebuild, and ship new binaries. Every secret that was in the environment of a past build whose output left the build machine should be treated as exposed. Jacob Finkelman first reported the issue in [#8802](https://github.com/RustPython/RustPyth…

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0402: Heap buffer overflow in `CCtx::try_clone` on a multithreaded context
entry.content:
Heap buffer overflow in `CCtx::try_clone` on a multithreaded context

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

`CCtx::try_clone` (`experimental` feature, deprecated) copies tables sized from the context's applied parameters. Starting a multithreaded frame (`zstdmt` feature) replaces those parameters with the workers' without resizing the context's own tables, so after an abandoned single-threaded frame, the copy wrote up to 512 KiB past a heap allocation, or read past one. This became reachable with the bundled zstd 1.5.6. The flaw was corrected by refusing `try_clone` (and the unsafe `compress_block`) once `NbWorkers` was set on the context.

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0405: Out-of-bounds read with an out-of-range `InBuffer::pos`
entry.content:
Out-of-bounds read with an out-of-range `InBuffer::pos`

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

`InBuffer`'s fields are public, so safe code can set `pos` past the end of `src`. The position was passed to the C library unchecked, and `ZSTD_seekable_compressStream`, unlike the other streaming functions, does not validate it: it read past the end of the input slice, by up to the frame size, and compressed that memory into the output. The flaw was corrected by checking the position before every call into the C library.

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0406: Use-after-free when changing a multithreaded context with an unfinished frame
entry.content:
Use-after-free when changing a multithreaded context with an unfinished frame

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

When a multithreaded frame (`zstdmt` feature, `CParameter::NbWorkers`) is left unfinished, its jobs may still be running on the worker threads: the C library only waits for them when the next frame starts, or when the context is freed. A session reset makes the context accept changes again in the meantime, so: - unloading the dictionary (`load_dictionary`, `ref_cdict`, `ref_prefix`, `disable_dictionary`, `init*`, or `reset` with parameters) freed the dictionary a worker was still compressing against; - changing `NbWorkers` made the next frame resize the job table before waiting for the old jobs. The flaw was corrected by refusing these calls while a multithreaded frame is unfinished. The new `CCtx::wait_for_workers()` waits for the workers first.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/zstd-safe
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0406.html
  • https://github.com/gyscos/zstd-rs/commit/e224018a2389915d68ed17f30109bebad36e9734

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0404: Double free in `DCtx::try_clone`
entry.content:
Double free in `DCtx::try_clone`

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

`DCtx::try_clone` (`experimental` feature, deprecated) is a plain copy of the C context. A context owning a dictionary (from `load_dictionary`, `ref_prefix` or `init_using_dict`) or a dictionary table (`ref_ddict` with `RefMultipleDDicts`) ended up with both copies freeing it. A context cloned mid-frame resumed on uninitialized stream state. The clone also silently lost the `WindowLogMax` limit. The flaw was corrected by refusing to clone such contexts, and by carrying over the parameters the copy leaves out.

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0398: `Seekable::decompress` sets a `Vec` length beyond its capacity for offsets past the end
entry.content:
`Seekable::decompress` sets a `Vec` length beyond its capacity for offsets past the end

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

`ZSTD_seekable_decompress` shortens the requested length to the end of the data without checking that the offset is before it. For an offset past the end, it returns a wrapped-around length without writing anything, and `Seekable::decompress` passed that length to `Vec::set_len`. With the `seekable` feature, whoever supplies the archive, or chooses the offset, can leave the caller's `Vec<u8>` with a length far beyond its capacity. Reading it then discloses neighbouring heap memory, and appending to it corrupts memory. Offsets near `u64::MAX` can also hang the call. The flaw was corrected by clamping requests to the end of the data, and by checking every count reported by the C library against the buffer capacity.

  • https://crates.io/crates/zstd-safe

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0411: Out-of-bounds read in `Log2Cache::nlog2n()`, `nlog2n_difference()` and `plog2p()`
entry.content:
Out-of-bounds read in `Log2Cache::nlog2n()`, `nlog2n_difference()` and `plog2p()`

Affected:

  • dahl-salso — fixed in 0.7.0

`Log2Cache::new(n)` fills its three tables with entries for `0..=n`, but the three accessor methods index those tables with `get_unchecked` on a value the caller supplies. Nothing bounds the argument and nothing documents a bound, so any value above the `n` the cache was built with reads past the end of the vector. `CountType` is `u32`, so the read can land up to `u32::MAX` elements away, and `plog2p()` returns the value it read, disclosing whatever lies there. For example, `Log2Cache::new(4)` builds tables holding 5 entries (indices 0,1,2,3,4). Then `cache.nlog2n(60000)` reads index 60000, far outside the allocation. Under AddressSanitizer this faults with `SEGV`; Miri reports it as undefined behavior at `src/log2cache.rs:42`. `nlog2n_difference()` is off by one further: in the affected…

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0397: `OutBuffer::around_pos` exposes uninitialized memory
entry.content:
`OutBuffer::around_pos` exposes uninitialized memory

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

`OutBuffer::around_pos` accepted a position past the initialized length of a `Vec<u8>`. The next streaming call then marked everything before the position as initialized, so safe code could read stale heap memory between the vector's previous length and that position. The flaw was corrected by zero-filling that gap.

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0391: Data from an abandoned stream leaks into the next stream on a reused context
entry.content:
Data from an abandoned stream leaks into the next stream on a reused context

Affected:

  • zstd — fixed in 0.14.3

The `with_context` constructors of the stream encoders and decoders used the borrowed context as it was. When a stream was abandoned on a context, for example an encoder dropped before `finish()` after an error, whatever it left there was carried into the next stream: the input buffered by the previous encoder (up to 128 KiB, or all of it with `zstdmt`) became the start of the next frame, and a decoder returned undelivered output of the previous stream. An application reusing one context for data that must stay separate, such as different users' requests, could disclose one user's plaintext to another. Whoever supplies the data can cause the abandonment with invalid input. The flaw was corrected by resetting the context's session in `with_context`.

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0393: Out-of-bounds read when training a dictionary from inconsistent sample sizes
entry.content:
Out-of-bounds read when training a dictionary from inconsistent sample sizes

Affected:

  • zstd — fixed in 0.4.10

`ZDICT_trainFromBuffer` is never told the length of the samples buffer. Before 0.4.10, `zstd::dict::from_continuous` (initially `train_dict`) called it directly: up to 0.2.1 without checking the sample sizes against the buffer at all, and from 0.3.0 with a sum that wraps around when overflow checks are off, as in release builds. Sizes that do not describe the buffer made the trainer read past its end. This requires the sample sizes to come from an untrusted source. From 0.4.10, training goes through zstd-safe, where the same flaw is covered by the zstd-safe advisory for it, fixed in zstd-safe 8.2.0.

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0401: Out-of-bounds read in `train_from_buffer` when sample sizes overflow
entry.content:
Out-of-bounds read in `train_from_buffer` when sample sizes overflow

Affected:

  • zstd-safe — fixed in 8.2.0

`ZDICT_trainFromBuffer` is never told the length of the samples buffer, so `train_from_buffer` checked that the sample sizes add up to it. With overflow checks off, as in release builds, that sum wrapped around: sizes totalling 2^64 plus the buffer length passed the check, and the trainer read past the end of the buffer. `zstd::dict::from_continuous` relies on this check from zstd 0.4.10; older versions of zstd had their own, covered by a separate advisory. This requires the sample sizes to come from an untrusted source. The flaw was corrected by summing the sizes with overflow checks.
